title: A systematic review of AI-driven intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) in K-12 education
extended_summary:
This systematic review examines how AI-driven intelligent tutoring systems (ITSs) have been evaluated in K-12 education and what effects they have on student learning and performance. The paper is motivated by the rapid growth of AI in education and the continued uncertainty about whether ITSs reliably improve outcomes, especially in school settings where evidence has been thinner than in higher education.

The review synthesizes 28 studies involving 4,597 students and focuses on the experimental designs used, the kinds of comparison conditions employed, and the reported learning outcomes. Across the included studies, the authors found that quasi-experimental designs were most common, typically using pre- and post-tests with an ITS condition contrasted against teacher-led instruction, non-intelligent tutoring systems, modified versions of the same ITS, or no control group. The studies covered elementary, middle, and high school learners, with most in mathematics and other STEM subjects, and a smaller number in language learning and writing.

Overall, the review concludes that ITSs generally show positive effects on K-12 learning and performance, but these effects are less clear when compared with non-intelligent tutoring systems or when interventions are brief and possibly influenced by novelty effects. The authors argue that personalization, adaptivity, immediate feedback, and teacher-supported blended use appear important for effectiveness, while also noting the field’s lack of attention to ethics and the need for longer, more diverse studies.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: An intelligent tutoring system is an AI-enabled educational software system that adapts instruction, feedback, pacing, and/or problem sequencing to a learner’s needs.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review of 28 K-12 studies evaluating AI-driven intelligent tutoring systems across subjects, grade levels, and comparison conditions.

findings.finding_summary: Across 28 K-12 studies (N=4597), the review found that ITS effects on learning and performance were generally positive. However, the positive effects were often weaker when ITSs were compared with non-intelligent tutoring systems, and study designs varied widely.
findings.measure: Student learning and performance outcomes across included K-12 studies

findings.finding_summary: In comparisons of ITS vs teacher-led instruction, seven of eight studies reported a significant positive effect favoring ITSs, typically with medium to large effects. In comparisons of ITS vs non-intelligent tutoring systems, only one of four studies showed an advantage for ITS; the other studies found no significant difference.
findings.measure: Learning gains and performance on pre/post tests across control conditions
findings.effect_size: varied; medium to large in ITS vs teacher studies; mostly null in ITS vs non-intelligent TS studies

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review synthesizing 28 quasi-experimental studies rather than a single controlled trial. The review includes a substantial sample size and clearly described comparison conditions, but the primary studies vary considerably in design, duration, and outcome measures.
impact_tier_rationale: The review reports generally positive effects, often medium to large when ITSs are compared with teacher-led instruction. However, effects are mixed or null against non-intelligent tutoring systems, so the overall impact is modest rather than unequivocal.
